$SYHBF $SYH.V #Uranium #Nuclear
One date in Skyharbour’s latest update caught my attention: 1989. ⚒️

That’s when the Little Man area at Getty East was last drilled before the current campaign.

Historical drilling outlined uranium mineralization along 500 metres. Skyharbour’s interpretation suggests it remains open in both directions, with the underlying basement rocks entirely untested.

Now Denison is funding a ~3,600m Getty East drill program, operated by Skyharbour, with four holes initially planned at Little Man.

Think about that: a known uranium occurrence, geological questions left unanswered for decades, and fresh drilling to investigate them.

The deeper exploration theme extends to the 100%-owned Moore project, where the 2026 program includes testing largely unexplored basement potential around Maverick’s high-grade mineralization.

That’s an aspect of $SYH I find particularly interesting. Modern exploration models can bring a different perspective to ground where earlier drilling established that uranium was present—and left plenty unresolved.

The drill bit still has to deliver. But these are concrete geological questions worth testing as the nuclear industry looks toward its future fuel needs.

Looking forward to @JordanPTrimble’s full RCTV interview. There’s a lot to discuss beneath the surface of Skyharbour’s Athabasca story.
